solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Atmosphere around college mostly productive? That's a crucial point

indicators.note: around tells us the atmosphere word wraps round the college letter

parts.note: climate is the prevailing atmosphere or mood, as in a climate of fear

indicators.note: mostly means take nearly all of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: rich soil is productive, fertile ground

explanation.surface: A query about whether the mood around a university is mostly fruitful, then a remark that this is the key issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A climacteric is a critical period or turning point, so it is a decisive moment.

clue.text: Boundless back pain holding blokes up in regard to filming

indicators.note: holding means the trimmed pain word wraps around the other piece
boundless means without its bounds, so the outer letters of the pain word go

parts.note: sciatica is pain running down the back and leg

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the blokes word is read bottom to top

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad back is propped up by fellows while talking about film work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' strips the outer letters off the pain word, and 'up' reads the blokes upwards before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinematic is the adjective relating to cinema, the art of making films.

clue.text: Coarse left-winger chasing one legal degree

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the left-winger follows the other pieces

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
LLB is the Bachelor of Laws degree
a red is a communist or socialist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: A vulgar socialist pursues a single law qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-bred people have bad manners, so they are rough and vulgar.

clue.text: Opposition to government elaborated in a march around Sunday

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the Sunday letter
elaborated means worked out or developed, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A protest against the state is spelt out during a Sunday march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborated' rearranges IN A MARCH, and 'around' puts that round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political belief that the state should be abolished.

clue.text: Seasons having day occupied by Cup matches? On the contrary

indicators.note: occupied by signals one piece sitting inside another
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the matches word holds the day letter

parts.note: cup ties are knockout matches in a cup competition

explanation.surface: Times of year when the calendar fills up with knockout football fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, D would hold TIES; 'On the contrary' flips that so TIES holds D. A tide is an old word for a season, as in Eastertide.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide survives as a word for a season or festival time, as in Yuletide and Whitsuntide.

clue.text: Animosity activated most of monarch's followers

parts.note: to run a machine is to operate it, so activated gives ran

indicators.note: most of means dropping the final letter of the followers word

parts.note: a court is the retinue that attends a king or queen

explanation.surface: Bad feeling stirred up among the king's entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment, much the same as hostility.

clue.text: Losing passion, losing any sign of love? Hold on

indicators.note: in tennis love is zero, written as the letter O, so every such letter goes

parts.note: cooling, as in cooling off, is losing ardour

explanation.surface: A fading romance, with the plea to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis scoring, shown by O; both Os are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly and not let go, which is to keep a firm grip.

clue.text: Last one to abandon top of spire?

indicators.note: to abandon means one piece leaves the other, so it is removed

parts.note: a finial is the ornament crowning a spire or gable
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A climber is the last one to leave the summit of a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of spire' looks like a first-letter instruction (S) but it defines the ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means coming at the end, the ultimate one in a series.

clue.text: Resist soft soap? One shouldn't

parts.note: to face down or confront something is to resist it
flannel is British slang for flattering or evasive talk, as is soft soap

explanation.surface: Advice not to stand up against flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: A face flannel is a small washcloth, so it ought to welcome soft soap rather than resist it.
explanation.definitionFit: A washcloth is used with soap on the skin, so it is the item that should never refuse lather.

clue.text: Piece of music with a note on it reversed

parts.note: with means and, joining things together

indicators.note: reversed means the words on it are read backwards

explanation.surface: A composition carrying a musical note that has been flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns ON IT into TINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a tempo marking and a movement played slightly faster than andante.

clue.text: Atom scientist's work with writer — I'm here for editing

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a pen is a writing tool, hence a writer

indicators.note: for editing means the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nuclear physicist's paper, co-written with an author who is on hand to revise it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for editing' rearranges I'M HERE into HEIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: J. Robert Oppenheimer directed the Manhattan Project that built the first nuclear bomb.

clue.text: Linen, cold material, not fine, swaddling male

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: swaddling means wrapping round, so the trimmed material wraps the male letter
not means the fine letter is left out

parts.note: fabric is cloth, material
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Fabric that is chilly and coarse being wrapped round a baby boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fine' takes F from FABRIC, leaving ABRIC, which wraps M.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white linen or cotton cloth.

clue.text: Jars filled by a doctor recalled in temporary measure

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole thing is read backwards
filled by means the other pieces go inside the jars word

parts.note: jars are pots
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: Containers stocked by a physician who was then summoned back as a short-term fix.
explanation.walkthrough: POTS holding A GP makes PAGPOTS; 'recalled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a makeshift that fills a need until something better arrives.

clue.text: Satisfied around half-time or raising a stink?

indicators.note: around means the satisfied word wraps the other piece

parts.note: having been fed, your hunger is satisfied

indicators.note: half here means only the first two of the four letters of time are used

explanation.surface: Was the crowd content at the interval, or were they making a fuss?
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the football break, but it means half of the word time. 'Raising a stink' is read literally, as giving off a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fetid smells foul, so it literally sends up a stench.

clue.text: Light switch without is turned on in wet situation

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the switch word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a dimmer is a switch that controls the brightness of a light

indicators.note: turned means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A lamp control with no outer case gets switched on in the damp, a dangerous idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes away the D of DIMMER, leaving IMMER; 'turned' makes SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersion is being plunged under water, so it is the state of being soaked.

clue.text: Employee of site defaced statement of intent

parts.note: a man can be a worker or employee, as in management and men

indicators.note: defaced means spoilt or disfigured, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A worker at the premises vandalised a mission statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' rearranges OF SITE into IFESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of aims, typically by a political party.

clue.text: I buy land for tilling around Institute (though not so as you'd hear)

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the institute letter
tilling means turning over soil, so the letters get turned over

explanation.surface: A farmer quietly buys ground to plough near a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for tilling' rearranges I BUY LAND, and 'around' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaudibly means too quietly to be heard, at a level below hearing.

clue.text: Newsreader presenting articles about Church coming by gold — millions

indicators.note: about means the articles go round the remaining pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, used twice for articles
or is gold in heraldry
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reports on pieces about a church that came into gold worth millions.
explanation.walkthrough: AN and AN go either side of CH, OR and M.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman presents a news programme and links its reports.

clue.text: Best drug involves time and money, variously

indicators.note: variously means the two inserted letters go in at different places
involves means the drug word takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug

explanation.surface: A narcotic that eats up hours and cash, in assorted ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variously' says the time and money letters go into the drug at two different places, not side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable or ideal, the finest possible.

clue.text: Mature student given work in Old English

indicators.note: in means the student piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a fag was a junior boy at a British public school made to do chores for a senior

explanation.surface: A grown-up learner set an assignment in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: At British boarding schools a fag was a younger pupil who ran errands for an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of age is to be legally an adult, fully grown up.

clue.text: Soldiers turned up on time in plant

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so these words go backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Troops arrived punctually inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrived, but it reverses ON AGE to EGANO. 'plant' is the herb, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, used in cooking.

clue.text: Identifying label: satisfied one is carried by badger

indicators.note: is carried by means the pieces are held inside the badger word

parts.note: to badger someone is to nag them
to meet a need is to satisfy it
a means one

explanation.surface: A tag satisfied by an animal, with a badger carrying ID.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge or label showing who someone is.

clue.text: Bananas? Starchy plant, nothing less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the nothing letter is taken out

parts.note: manioc is cassava, a starchy root crop
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Are bananas a starchy plant, minus nothing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for wildly excited or mad, as is manic.

clue.text: Newspaper upset lawyer and policeman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the newspaper word is turned upside down

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A tabloid annoyed both a solicitor and a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like annoyed but reverses RAG. The Garda is the Irish police force, and a member is a garda.
explanation.definitionFit: A garda is an officer of the Garda Síochána, the police of Ireland.

clue.text: Province's expression of disapproval following return of government department

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
F is the abbreviation for following, as in pages

indicators.note: return of means the department word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: the MoD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A region's tut-tutting after a ministry is brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a position word but supplies F. The MoD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiefdom is an area under one person's control, a domain or territory.

clue.text: Consecutive letters on chests forming identifying features

parts.note: L and M sit next to each other in the alphabet, read as L AND M
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Successive initials stamped on boxes make them recognisable.
explanation.walkthrough: The consecutive letters are spoken in full, L and M, so the joining word is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Landmarks are prominent features that help you recognise where you are.

clue.text: Stone room church has abandoned

indicators.note: has abandoned means the church letters have left the room word

parts.note: a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A stone-walled room that the congregation has deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Amber is fossil resin, counted as a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin used as a gem, treated as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Musical activity's affected, along with half of your dancing

parts.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner

indicators.note: dancing means the letters jump about into a new order
half of means take the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: Someone's showy style, along with half your dance moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives YO from your; 'dancing' rearranges ALONG plus YO into ANOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanology is the art of bell-ringing, a musical pursuit.
